expansion:
A. Observation and reassurance is correct. This is an uncomplicated complete posterior vitreous detachment: the Weiss ring supports separation of the posterior vitreous, and the careful examination has found no retinal tear, hole, or vitreoretinal traction. In this setting, reassurance with retinal-detachment warning advice and follow-up is appropriate (not taken from the course material). The lecture does not teach posterior vitreous detachment or Weiss ring; it states only that aging may cause “vitreous shrinkage” (L20, slide 6).

B. Prophylactic barrier laser photocoagulation is wrong because there is no retinal break to surround. Laser retinopexy is used to secure selected retinal tears or breaks, not an uncomplicated posterior vitreous detachment with an intact retina (not taken from the course material). The lecture does not cover prophylactic laser for a break without detachment. Its laser reference is in pneumatic retinopexy, where a gas bubble seals a tear and is “often followed by LASER OR CRYOTHERAPY (FREEZING)” (L20, slide 14).

C. Pars plana vitrectomy is wrong because there is neither a retinal detachment nor traction requiring operative relief. The lecture describes vitrectomy for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment as removal of vitreous with a gas or oil bubble to push the retina back (L20, slide 14), and for tractional detachment with membrane peeling to remove pulling fibrovascular tissue (L20, slide 15). Neither indication is present here.

D. Scleral buckling is wrong because it is a repair for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment associated with a retinal break, not for isolated posterior vitreous detachment. The lecture says that surgery is almost always required to seal the retinal break in rhegmatogenous detachment and describes scleral buckling as a silicone band that helps the retina reattach (L20, slide 14). This patient has no break and no detachment.
objective: Recognize that an uncomplicated posterior vitreous detachment with no retinal break or traction is managed conservatively with observation and reassurance.
